# vendor/aqa/server — aqa_server automation daemon

Native C++17 daemon exposing an HTTP/JSON REST API so the device can be driven
from any host on the same network. Started by init from `aqa_server.rc`, built
by `Android.bp`, installed to `/system/bin/aqa_server`.

> **This is one of two control planes on a qalos image.** The other is the
> framework-level `RemoteControlService` (`packages/apps/RemoteControlService/`,
> port **9000**, inside `system_server`). See
> ["Relationship to RemoteControlService"](#relationship-to-remotecontrolservice)
> below — read that before adding endpoints here.

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Method | Body / query | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/v1/health` | GET | — | `{"ok":true,"port":8080}` — **unauthenticated** |
| `/v1/display` | GET | — | `{"width":1440,"height":3120}` |
| `/v1/foreground` | GET | `?raw=1` | `{"component":"com.pkg/.Act"}`, plus `raw` when asked |
| `/v1/screenshot` | GET | — | full-resolution PNG, `Content-Type: image/png` |
| `/v1/ui/dump` | GET | — | window hierarchy as XML, `Content-Type: application/xml` |
| `/v1/sms/inbox` | GET | `?raw=1` | `{"messages":[{"address","body","date"}...]}` |
| `/v1/tap` | POST | `{"x":int,"y":int}` | `{"ok":true}` |
| `/v1/swipe` | POST | `{"x1","y1","x2","y2","duration_ms"}` | `{"ok":true}` |
| `/v1/key` | POST | `{"keycode":int}` | `{"ok":true}` |
| `/v1/type` | POST | `{"text":string}` | `{"ok":true,"out":"..."}` |
| `/v1/app/start` | POST | `{"package","activity"}` | `{"ok":true,"out":"..."}` |
| `/v1/app/stop` | POST | `{"package":string}` | `{"ok":true}` |

### Errors

Every error uses the **same envelope as RemoteControlService**, so one client
error path works against either port:

```json
{"code":"MISSING_FIELD","message":"x is required","field":"x"}
```

| Status | `code` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `MISSING_FIELD` | required field absent or not numeric |
| 400 | `LAUNCH_FAILED` | `am start` refused the component (see `out`) |
| 401 | `UNAUTHORIZED` | off-box request without a valid `Authorization` header |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | unknown path |
| 500 | `SCREENCAP_FAILED` | `screencap` produced no output |
| 500 | `UI_DUMP_FAILED` | `uiautomator dump` produced no file |

`/v1/app/start` is the only endpoint that inspects command *output* rather
than exit status, because `am` exits 0 even for a component that does not
exist. Treat 400 `LAUNCH_FAILED` as real.

## Authentication

Identical contract to `RemoteControlService`:

- **Bearer token** at `/data/local/tmp/qalos_token` (auto-generated by
  RemoteControlService on first boot, 64 hex chars, mode 0644).
- **Loopback clients are trusted** and skip the token check — same-device
  access via `adb forward`.
- **Non-loopback clients** must send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Comparison is constant-time; there is no early exit on a mismatching byte.
- **A missing/empty token file rejects every off-box request.** That is the
  safe failure mode, not an open door.

```bash
TOKEN=$(adb shell cat /data/local/tmp/qalos_token)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://<device-ip>:8080/v1/display
```

## Relationship to RemoteControlService

Two REST servers run on an AQA image. That split is deliberate but must be
kept consistent:

| | `aqa_server` (this) | `RemoteControlService` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where | init service, `user root` | inside `system_server` |
| Port | 8080 | 9000 |
| SELinux | `u:r:su:s0` | normal system_server domain |
| Shipped in | AQA products only | **every** product that ran `apply-qalos.sh` |
| Auth | shared bearer token, loopback trusted | same |
| Error shape | `{code,message,field}` | same |
| Audit | logcat tag `aqa_audit` | native event capture (legal/AGENTS.md 2.9) |
| Screenshot scaling | not implemented (full res only) | `?width=&height=` supported |
| Extra surface | `/v1/ui/dump` (uiautomator) | long-press, pinch, force-stop by name |

**Consequences to respect:**

1. **Do not invent a new error shape or auth rule here.** A client that handles
   one port's 401 must handle the other's.
2. **Keep `kTokenPath` in sync** with `RemoteControlService.TOKEN_PATH`.
3. **`/v1/ui/dump` exists only here.** Frame the JSON/XML conventions the same
   way if it is ever added to RemoteControlService.
4. **Two servers means two ports to firewall.** Neither is safe on an untrusted
   network — the root one especially.

Longer term this should collapse to one plane. Tracking that decision is
deliberately left open (see `vendor/aqa/README.md`), because deleting either
service changes the audit-log story.

## Architecture

```text
aqa_server  (init service, class=main, user=root, seclabel=u:r:su:s0)
├── HttpServer            0.0.0.0:8080, single-threaded accept loop
│     ├── authorized()    loopback trusted, else Bearer token
│     └── dispatch()      route on path, JSON-scan the body
├── UInputInjector        /dev/uinput, BUS_VIRTUAL multi-touch digitizer
└── shell-outs to         /system/bin/{input,am,content,screencap,uiautomator,dumpsys,grep}
```

**Input mechanism is deliberately mixed.** `tap` / `swipe` / `key` go through
`/dev/uinput` so they work with the screen off and are not subject to
`input(1)` quirks. `type` is a shell-out to `input text`, because per-keycode
injection cannot produce arbitrary Unicode.

**Signal handling.** `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` are blocked with `pthread_sigmask()`
*before* the accept thread is created, then consumed with `sigwait()`. Blocking
afterwards leaves the default disposition in place and the process is killed
from an arbitrary thread. `SIGPIPE` is ignored so a client disconnecting
mid-response cannot take the daemon down.

**`/dev/uinput` needs no ueventd rule** — the daemon runs as root, so it can
open the node whatever its mode. An earlier revision copied a fragment over
`$(TARGET_COPY_OUT_VENDOR)/etc/ueventd.rc`, which would have clobbered
pantah's own rules.

## Audit logging

Every state-changing request (`tap`, `swipe`, `key`, `type`, `app/start`,
`app/stop`) and every rejected auth attempt is written to logcat under the
tag **`aqa_audit`**, with the client address:

```bash
adb logcat -s aqa_audit
```

This is the on-device substrate `legal/AGENTS.md` §2.9 requires. It is *not* a
durable audit log — logcat rotates. A commercial fleet needs the store
described in `legal/AUDIT_LOGGING.md`.

## Host smoke test

The read-only endpoints need no device hardware, so the daemon can be compiled
and partially exercised on a Linux host. `main.cpp` guards its `android/log.h`
include, so plain `g++` works:

```bash
g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -pthread src/main.cpp src/uinput_injector.cpp src/http_server.cpp -o aqa_server
./aqa_server                     # /dev/uinput init fails; endpoints still serve
curl -s localhost:8080/v1/health
curl -s localhost:8080/v1/display
```

On device:

```bash
TOKEN=$(adb shell cat /data/local/tmp/qalos_token)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://<device-ip>:8080/v1/screenshot -o screen.png
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://<device-ip>:8080/v1/ui/dump > ui.xml
```

## Limitations

- **No TLS.** Bearer tokens cross the wire in clear text on an untrusted
  network. Bind to a private network or restrict with iptables.
- **No rate limiting.**
- **Single-threaded accept loop.** Blocking shell-outs serialise requests; a
  hung `am` or `uiautomator` stalls the whole loop.
- **Flat JSON scanner, not a parser:** no nesting, no handling of `\"` escaped
  quotes inside string values.
- **Screenshot scaling is not implemented** (see the comparison table).
- **`/v1/sms/inbox` field slicing is a heuristic.** `content query` emits
  unquoted `key=value, key=value` rows, so a body containing a literal
  `, date=` or `, body=` mis-splits. Use `?raw=1` when that matters.
- **`/v1/foreground` is best-effort.** It greps `dumpsys activity` then
  `dumpsys window`; the shape differs between releases and the component
  string may be empty on an unusual window stack.
